items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear and the formatting matches the file. The new make_msgid has a docstring, but it is copied almost word for word from the stdlib email.utils.make_msgid, which is a minor issue.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The `.encode('idna').decode('ascii')` call is pasted inline in both utils.get_fqdn and the new make_msgid instead of a shared helper. The wrapper is mostly redundant once DNS_NAME is fixed, and it replaces the make_msgid exported by django.core.mail, changing its default domain.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No errors are swallowed and no try/except hides failures. A bad domain raises UnicodeError, the same as the reference. ASCII names pass through unchanged, and encoding a name twice is idempotent.

items.name: Conversion is encoding-independent and safe for ASCII names
items.name_zh: 转换与编码无关且不影响 ASCII 主机名
items.evidence: The domain is converted at the source (`socket.getfqdn().encode('idna').decode('ascii')`), which works for every encoding. But the same idna conversion is repeated in the make_msgid wrapper (`str(domain).encode('idna')...`), so it is duplicated inline instead of using one helper.
